warnings.summary: Keep the distinction between tree survival and successful flowering or fruiting.

importantNotes.value: UF/IFAS describes dry weather before and during bloom as favorable. This is an optimum, not proof of a universal dry-season requirement. Keep this qualification; do not infer requiresDrySeason=true.

sunNeeds.shortExcerpt: Full sun is recommended for growth and fruit production.

waterNeeds.shortExcerpt: Irrigate establishment and prolonged drought; mature trees should not receive frequent watering.

coldTolerance.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS lists the USDA hardiness band as 10B through 11.
coldTolerance.interpretation: Keep the existing ordinal; replace generic heuristic provenance with explicit zone evidence and the existing approved transform.

heatTolerance.shortExcerpt: Table 10 reports mango heat damage above 104 degrees Fahrenheit and an optimum growing range of 75 to 86 degrees Fahrenheit.
heatTolerance.interpretation: Proposed conservative CRUVIT qualitative category, NOT the source's literal ordinal and NOT a universal damage-free survival boundary. It retains extreme-heat constraint in the current evaluator.

frostSensitivity.shortExcerpt: Young trees can die near freezing; flowers and small fruits suffer cold injury above freezing.

needsWinterChill.shortExcerpt: Not established as a universal species-level category by the reviewed source.

groupIds.shortExcerpt: Structural group retained from explicit hot/arid palm production ecology.

sunNeeds.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS states date palm requires full sun for optimal growth.

waterNeeds.shortExcerpt: Date palms need ample water/groundwater while fruit production favors arid weather.

warningFlags.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS notes 3-4 inch thorns formed by modified leaflets on the petiole.

coldTolerance.shortExcerpt: Mississippi State Extension lists Phoenix dactylifera as USDA zone 8b and reports hardiness around 12°F.

drainageNeeds.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS recommends neutral to acidic, well-drained soils.

heatTolerance.shortExcerpt: UC Cooperative Extension states date fruit production needs high heat and arid weather.

hardBlockRules.shortExcerpt: Very large mature palm size supports a no-small-container placement rule.

frostSensitivity.shortExcerpt: Leaves can burn near 20°F and plants may be killed near 10°F; whole-plant frost sensitivity retained as medium.

humidityTolerance.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS says date palm prefers dry climates but also occurs in humid Florida; fruiting under Gulf Coast humidity is cultivar-limited.

fruitingRequirements.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS documents edible dates and both-sex requirement; UC Extension states high heat and arid weather are needed to produce fruit.

floweringRequirements.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS and University of Arizona describe separate male and female plants and flowers.

survivalVsThriveNotes.shortExcerpt: Survival/landscape growth is broader than commercial fruit production climate.

reproductive.dioecious.shortExcerpt: Date palms are dioecious, with separate male and female plants.

reproductive.sex_requirement.shortExcerpt: Both male and female plants are needed for reliable date fruit production.

reproductive.cultivar_dependency.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS notes hundreds of date palm varieties and strong differences in fruiting under humid Gulf Coast conditions.

reproductive.requires_pollinator.shortExcerpt: Fruit production requires female and male trees in the same area.

reproductive.compatible_pollinator_requi.shortExcerpt: University of Arizona notes pollen is transferred from male flowers to female plants and cultivation may use manual pollination.

sourceReviews.note: No quantified or explicit boolean winter-chill requirement found in this reviewed source. Absence of a statement is NOT proof of false.

needsWinterChill.interpretation: The reviewed sources did not establish a universal winter-chill boolean. UNKNOWN is retained; absence of a statement is not evidence of false.

fruiting.sourceExcerpt: Edible date production needs male and female trees, hot dry weather, and adequate water; humid climates can sharply limit productive cultivars. UF/IFAS documents edible dates and both-sex requirement; UC Extension states high heat and arid weather are needed to produce fruit.
sourceExcerpts: Edible date production needs male and female trees, hot dry weather, and adequate water; humid climates can sharply limit productive cultivars. UF/IFAS documents edible dates and both-sex requirement; UC Extension states high heat and arid weather are needed to produce fruit.

climate_traits.fruitingRequirements: Edible date production needs male and female trees, hot dry weather, and adequate water; humid climates can sharply limit productive cultivars.
climate_traits.floweringRequirements: Male and female flowers occur on separate trees; both sexes are needed in the area for fruit production.
climate_traits.survivalVsThriveNotes: The palm can grow in some humid or marginal climates, but reliable edible fruit production is much narrower and favors hot arid conditions with adequate irrigation.

after.fruiting_requirements: Edible date production needs male and female trees, hot dry weather, and adequate water; humid climates can sharply limit productive cultivars.
after.flowering_requirements: Male and female flowers occur on separate trees; both sexes are needed in the area for fruit production.

groupIds.shortExcerpt: Structural groups reflect documented houseplant, climbing support, toxicity, and fruit-crop roles.

sunNeeds.shortExcerpt: NCSU lists dappled sunlight and partial shade; fruit production may use more sun.

waterNeeds.shortExcerpt: Water thoroughly then allow partial drying; periodic irrigation improves growth and fruit.

warningFlags.shortExcerpt: All plant parts and unripe fruit contain irritating calcium oxalate; only ripe fruit pulp is edible.

drainageNeeds.shortExcerpt: NCSU and UF/IFAS require good drainage and warn against flooded/excessively wet soil.

heatTolerance.shortExcerpt: Warm tropical growth is preferred, but exposed full sun can scorch foliage; retained as medium heat tolerance.

hardBlockRules.shortExcerpt: NCSU states sturdy support is necessary to prevent stems from breaking.

frostSensitivity.shortExcerpt: Warm 60–85°F preference and USDA zones 10a–12b support high frost sensitivity as an explicit heuristic.

humidityTolerance.shortExcerpt: NCSU states Monstera deliciosa prefers high humidity.

fruitingRequirements.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS documents fruit maturation, edible ripe pulp, and calcium-oxalate hazard in unripe fruit.

floweringRequirements.shortExcerpt: NCSU and UF/IFAS document inflorescences and note flowering is rare in interior cultivation.

survivalVsThriveNotes.shortExcerpt: Survival/ornamental use is broader than fruiting outcome.

reproductive.self_fertile.shortExcerpt: UF/IFAS states the flowers are self-pollinating.

sourceReviews.note: No quantified or explicit boolean winter-chill requirement found in this reviewed source. Absence of a statement is NOT proof of false.
Reviewed without establishing a species-wide winter-chill boolean.

needsWinterChill.interpretation: The reviewed sources did not establish a universal winter-chill boolean. UNKNOWN is retained; absence of a statement is not evidence of false.

fruiting.sourceExcerpt: Fruit production is an outdoor warm-climate outcome; fruit takes about 12–14 months to mature and only fully ripe pulp should be eaten. UF/IFAS documents fruit maturation, edible ripe pulp, and calcium-oxalate hazard in unripe fruit.

climate_traits.fruitingRequirements: Fruit production is an outdoor warm-climate outcome; fruit takes about 12–14 months to mature and only fully ripe pulp should be eaten.
climate_traits.floweringRequirements: Mature outdoor vines in warm tropical or warm-subtropical conditions can produce a spadix/spathe; flowering is rare indoors.
climate_traits.survivalVsThriveNotes: Indoor foliage survival is much broader than reliable fruit production; fruiting needs mature outdoor growth in a warm climate and ripe-fruit safety handling.

after.fruiting_requirements: Fruit production is an outdoor warm-climate outcome; fruit takes about 12–14 months to mature and only fully ripe pulp should be eaten.
after.flowering_requirements: Mature outdoor vines in warm tropical or warm-subtropical conditions can produce a spadix/spathe; flowering is rare indoors.
